stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,re,json
from collections import Counter
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G

            while k>=0 and g[k][j]==bg: k-=1

def both2(g):
    H=len(g);W=len(g[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in g for x in r)
    bg=max(cnt,key=lambda v:cnt[v]); others={k:v for k,v in cnt.items() if k!=bg}
    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if g[i][j]!=bg: continue
            L=any(g[i][k] in others for k in range(j))
            R=any(g[i][k] in others for k in range(j+1,W))
            U=any(g[k][j] in others for k in range(i))
            D=any(g[k][j] in others for k in range(i+1,H))
            # require: (left and right) or (up and down)? plus maybe also the "between" sense: nearest?
            cond=(L and R) or (U and D)
            out[i][j]=2 if cond else out[i][j]
    return out

steps.text:
Demo 7: bg=1, wall=3. Filled cells are bg cells strictly between two walls in their row AND column? Check (16,2): row16 has 3 at cols 0 and 5; col2 has 3 at rows 16 and 23. Both → filled ✓. (18,1): col1 has 3 at 16,17,19,20,21,22,23; row18 no 3! Yet filled. Hmm. But (18,7) filled: row18 no 3, col7 has 3 at 16,20,21,22. So vertical only? And (17,7): row17 no 3, col7 yes. So demo7: fill iff cell lies between two 3s in its column (vertically), OR row? (16,2): row also between. Hmm mixed.

Check (16,6): row16 3s at 0,5; col6: 3s at 16,23. filled. (16,4): row between (cols 0,5). col4: 3 at 16,23? col4: row16='1', row23='1'? gi[23]='131113111': col4='1'. No. Yet filled via row ✓.

So rule might be: fill iff between two walls in row OR column (strictly), with both-or-union. Earlier union gave wrong counts... but those earlier attempts used "L/R/U/D existence" where L=bool(L) meaning any wall on that side — same as strictly-between since strictly between = left exists & right exists. Union over all pairs gave diffs? Maybe earlier failure was due to flood-fill vs strict-between confusion. Actually earlier attempt "(L and R) or (U and D)" broad version failed badly (228+ on demo3?). That IS exactly this union. Unless I misremember—summary said broad version `(L and R) or (U and D)` had many diffs... hmm.

Wait demo3 pair: earlier collect showed (True,True,False,False): [15,6] filled 15 of 21 unfilled... meaning union predicts many wrong. So pure strictly-between isn't right. Need something else.

But maybe direction matters: "fill iff strictly between in BOTH dimensions OR ..."? Test each combination per-pair with candidate predicates programmatically instead of guessing. Let me do a systematic search over predicates built from booleans (L,R,U,D + combinations + distances) using sklearn-ish brute force across all demos together.

from collections import Counter
def f(g):
    H=len(g); W=len(g[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in g for x in r)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]; wall=cnt.most_common(2)[1][0]
    # collect wall positions per row and col (any, including non-wall colors treated as walls)
    O=set(cnt)-{bg}
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    rw=[[k for k,x in enumerate(r) if x in O] for r in g]
    cw=[[k for k,x in enumerate([g[k][j] for k in range(H)]) if x in O] for j in range(W)]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if g[i][j]==bg:
                R_w=any(k<j for k in rw[i]) and any(k>j for k in rw[i])
                C_w=any(k<i for k in cw[j]) and any(k>i for k in cw[j])
                if R_w or C_w: out[i][j]=2
    return out
for p in [2,3,4,5,6,7,8]:
    pred=f(G[f'Demo pair {p} input']); go=G[f'Demo pair {p} output']
    diffs=[(i,j,pred[i][j],go[i][j]) for i in range(len(pred)) for j in range(len(pred[0])) if pred[i][j]!=go[i][j]]
    print(p,'diffs:',len(diffs), diffs[:6])
